data.content_ref: inline:The universal grammar counter-conditions across the neighbourhood (SRC_001, SRC_002, SRC_004) are mutually incompatible in their eval-observation thresholds: SRC_002 requires the rival translation to yield 'simpler or more unifying' patterns, while SRC_004 requires only 'tractable synthesis', meaning a grammar can satisfy both only if tractability implies unification. This abstracts the neighbourhood's counterconditions into a single dependence: SRC_004 reduces to SRC_002 if and only if P-tractability implies Q-unification. It is refuted if a lineage's grammar can tractably synthesize a rival primitive without producing a unifying structural pattern, breaking the reduction and leaving SRC_004's efficiency trade-off independent of SRC_002's epistemic loss.
